findings.what: Not every emitter has every ray visibility on. In all 28 frames, key, fill, kick, horn and their floor copies are hidden from reflection and transmission rays, and the four paper lamps are hidden from reflection rays. Each softbox's reflection is a separate glowing face that only reflections and the view through glass can see and that lights nothing: a specular-only emitter. In the 14 OFF frames the face plus the lamp carry the same light as one softbox, so they are a fair stand-in (note). In the 14 LIT frames the faces are switched off too (HOUSE_SOFTBOX_SEEN=0). The studio then leaves no reflection on any shell, cap or base and sends no light through any acrylic; the lamps get studio light only from the paper and the room walls. A real studio can do that only with flags, and the flags would cast shadows that the render does not have.

verdicts.reasoning:
The mark is real and sits where the critic says. I measured each bar against the ball beside it (x 760-790 and 850-880, y 1150-1195). Poison: upper bar dL* -1.11 (dE00 1.41), lower bar dL* -1.64 (dE00 1.58). Ice: -0.43 (0.54) and -1.14 (0.96). The other five tints are 0.3-0.8 dE00, which is the grain level. The contrast stays the same at 1200 and 800 px (Poison -1.09/-1.62 and -1.10/-1.62); only the size shrinks. So it is plain at 1:1 and at 1200 px, and at 800 px it is a faint smudge you can find if you look at the ball. It is absent in LIT-c and faint in LIT-g's Ember (G -1/+1/-1 levels).

The cause is only half right. I ray-traced the Core camera using the honest-light rig rebuild (ball centre z 0.107 m, R 80 mm). The trace puts the spot's mirror point at x 819-822, y 1156-1158, where LIT-f's speck was. In that trace the top card's upper face lands exactly on the upper bar (x 799-841, y 1156-1168). The flag (HOUSE_BOUNCE_CUT) never shows: its mirror image (x 805-836, y 1160-1166) falls entirely inside the top card's. The lower bar (x 799-840, y 1174-1190) is the floor under the two cards, 1-10 cm out, which the cards shade. The ball sees it through the 2.6-3.4 cm of space under their far ends. The light line is the floor between the spot and the cards' near edge, not the 7 mm slot between the cards. As seen from the ball, the spot is about 19 degrees below the camera (camera +9.0, spot -9.8 degrees elevation), not 22.

Narrowing the cards still works, because a narrower card also shades a narrower strip of floor. But the gain is about a third, not half. With cards 3.8 cm and 2.5 cm wide (the beam is 3.2 cm and 1.9 cm wide at the cards' far ends, plus 0.6 cm for the 3 mm emitter), the card's image narrows from 43 to 27 px and the shaded floor from 42 to 27 px. Giving the top card a floor-toned top face (black underneath) would remove the upper bar; the floor shadow would stay.
